title: Hungarian People's Republic
capsule: The Hungarian People's Republic (Magyar Népköztársaság) was the socialist state that governed Hungary; the dataset window opens in 1946, when the postwar Second Hungarian Republic was already being hollowed out by the Hungarian Communist Party's 'salami tactics' under Mátyás Rákosi, before the People's Republic was formally proclaimed with the Soviet-modeled constitution of 20 August 1949. The 1956 Revolution briefly overthrew party rule in October–November 1956 until Soviet forces crushed it, installed János Kádár, and executed Prime Minister Imre Nagy in 1958. Kádár's subsequent 'goulash communism' introduced limited market mechanisms and consumer goods, giving Hungary a comparatively high living standard within the Eastern Bloc. The People's Republic was dissolved on 23 October 1989, when the constitution was amended to rename the state the Republic of Hungary, leading to free multi-party elections in spring 1990.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Hungary's territory under the People's Republic was coterminous with post-Trianon Hungary, fixed by the 1947 Paris Peace Treaty, and is precisely documented.
